groups.text: It is currently 19 degrees and mostly clear in Berlin-Tempelhof.
With the morning weather set, here is the news.

PyTorch developers are resolving a technical failure in the software's core processing. A recent update that added a C++ stack meta kernel inadvertently triggered a RuntimeError, specifically noting that SymIntArrayRef expected to contain only concrete integers. This error occurred because view operations were being routed to a C++ meta kernel that was not aware of symints. To fix this, developers have implemented a forward fix to route these operations back to the existing kernel that handles symints correctly. The resolution comes through Pull Request 189447, which includes new tests to prevent the error from returning. This technical correction has been approved by contributors ezyang, AmesingFlank, and Skylion007. These changes ensure that the underlying machine learning framework can properly handle symbolic integers without crashing during execution.

The Bayeux Tapestry has returned to British soil for the first time in nearly a millennium. In a secretive operation during the early morning hours this Friday, a metal case holding the eleventh-century masterpiece was unloaded from a truck at the British Museum. Director Nicholas Cullinan called it a unique moment as museum staff and diplomats broke into applause. The UNESCO-listed work is stitched in wool on linen and depicts William the Conqueror crossing the Channel to defeat King Harald at the Battle of Hastings in 1066. While the tapestry was sewn by women in England, it spent centuries in Bayeux, France, serving as a symbol of the intertwined and often frictional history between the two nations. The exhibition opens on September 10 and runs until July 2027. Public interest is already high, with some 100,000 tickets sold on the first day of sales this month.

In Germany, the former inner-German border has been transformed into a nature reserve known as the Green Band. Environmental Minister Carsten Schneider recently visited the site, which stretches nearly 1,400 kilometers and varies between 50 and 200 meters in width. Once a death strip designed to prevent East Germans from fleeing to the West, this corridor now serves as a habitat for 7,500 partially endangered species of insects and spiders. Andreas Heil of the Environment Ministry describes the area as a connecting element rather than the dividing line it was during the Cold War. Meanwhile, in Ukraine, the Russian army continues its campaign against Ukrainian books. In a separate administrative matter, an audit by the Chamber of Accounts into the activities of the State Committee for Television and Radio Broadcasting is ongoing through August 2026, following an expansion of the committee's powers earlier this year.

Meta is aggressively pricing its new Muse Spark 1.1 AI model to compete with heavyweights like GPT-5.5 and Opus 4.8. Following the disappointment of older Llama models, Mark Zuckerberg invested heavily in infrastructure and the Meta Superintelligence Labs led by Alexandr Wang. This latest version introduces a public preview API for developers to prototype integrations and handle agentic tasks such as coding and computer navigation. In Africa, the payments unicorn Flutterwave has secured an undisclosed investment from Circle Ventures. The funding helps Flutterwave embed USDC settlement into existing business payment flows to reduce costs and bypass traditional banking hours. Meanwhile, in the luxury travel sector, Four Seasons Resorts of Asia is launching a curated collection of babymoon experiences across Thailand and Malaysia. These offerings focus on mindfulness and holistic healing for expectant parents, contrasting with the technical push toward agentic AI and digital financial infrastructure seen elsewhere.

The latest release of llama.cpp introduces several technical shifts for developers running local AI models. The most visible change is the addition of an output option to the command line interface. Support varies across hardware platforms, with macOS Apple Silicon and Intel versions available alongside iOS XCFrameworks. On Linux, the update provides builds for Ubuntu x64 and arm64 using CPU, Vulkan, ROCm 7.2, and OpenVINO. Windows users can now access CUDA 12.4 and 13.3 DLLs, as well as SYCL and HIP options. Android arm64 CPU support is also included in this version. However, some configurations remain unavailable; specifically, the KleidiAI enabled build for Apple Silicon and certain openEuler versions are currently disabled. These updates expand how users deploy models across different operating systems, though they leave specific hardware optimizations offline for now.

France has advanced to the World Cup semi-finals for the third consecutive time. On Thursday, Didier Deschamps' side faced a difficult start, struggling for the first forty-five minutes against a stubborn Moroccan defence. The deadlock finally broke in the second half when Kylian Mbappé and Ousmane Dembélé secured a two-zero victory for Les Bleus. This win ensures France moves forward in the tournament. They now wait to see who they will face for a spot in the final, with either Spain or Belgium remaining as their potential opponents.

India is turning toward coal-fired power to offset a decline in hydropower generation caused by warmer June temperatures and developing El Niño conditions. According to S&P Global, India's average hydropower generation fell by 6.3 average gigawatts this June while electricity demand rose by over 24 gigawatts, leaving the country among the most affected in Asia. Meanwhile, Google is facing legal challenges in India, appealing a Delhi High Court ruling that held the company liable for trademark infringement regarding keyword advertising. Google argues that keywords are merely backend triggers and warns that the ruling makes India a global outlier, potentially granting trademark owners a monopoly over advertising space. On the technical front, Google is expanding transparency for its users by generalizing labels for AI-generated ads across Search, Discover, and YouTube. The company will now include a "How this app is made" category in ad preferences to indicate if content was created or edited using generative AI.
After the headlines, back to the weather.
This afternoon will be cloudy with temperatures between 23 and 26 degrees.
And from the weather, a quick look at the calendar.

On your calendar today: Your work calendar has Soofi Evaluation at nine in the morning, NAS Brainstorm at one in the afternoon, Nilima Exit Interview at two thirty, and beer and cocktails at five. Your personal calendar has summer holidays in Berlin all day, Bubatz delivery at six, and Höfische at seven.
And that's it for your personal morning broadcast.
[mature adult voice, intensely emotional, tender, radiant; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
[very very long pause before speaking; then mature adult voice, most emotional, strong, warm, radiant, deeply encouraging; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
